course_summary:
ISEN 645 | Lean Engineering | Spring 2026
Instructor: Dr. Michael Do | mddo@tamu.edu
Grading: Class Discussions [25%], Assignments [15%], Practical Exercises (2x) [30%], Final Exam [30%] — A: 90-100%, B: 80-89.9%, C: 70-79.9%, D: 60-69.9%, F: below 60%
Topics: Gemba Kaizen, Kata, Lean 6σ DMAIC, Lenses of Lean, Engineering the Cell - Flow, Engineering for Variability in the PS Flow, Lean Supply Chain, Engineering the Value Stream for Flow, Engineering the Value Stream for Control, Controlling the Flow, Characterizing Value in the Value Stream, 6σ (variability reduction), LPS design, lean manufacturing cell design, PS 'health' monitoring, waste accounting, factory physics methods, SE architecture, lean production system (LPS), lean-6σ culture, lean manufacturing quantitative modeling methodologies, core principles of lean production systems, principles of lean thinking, modern manufacturing systems, philosophical requirements, managerial requirements, organizational requirements, case study analysis, systems engineering, methods, models, production systems, interdependencies, knowledge, skills, experiences (KSEs), lean engineering, systems thinking, value, value stream, flow, control, perfection, reduce variation, systems operations, Culture
Tools: Canvas
Prerequisites: ISEN 609 or by approval of instructor
